_comment: Step waterfall for one formula run, built from the step records af exports itself.
name: step-waterfall
title: Step duration by formula run
description: How long each step of a formula run took, in order, with the agent and model that ran it. Built from af's own step records. Only closed steps appear: a step that is still running, or that crashed, has no end and therefore no duration - inventing one would put a fabricated number where nothing could later distinguish it from a measurement.
af_decision_o4: O-4 (view delivery) is hybrid: files on disk plus a best-effort dashboard push. See README.md.
af_assumptions: COLUMN SPELLINGS AND JOIN VERIFIED AGAINST A LIVE BACKEND, THIS QUERY NOT EXECUTED: during review of PR #567 OpenObserve v0.91.3 was stood up from the pinned artifact and the per-step token view's query was run verbatim, confirming the ingest naming this view also relies on. This view's own query was NOT among those executed. That live run observed af_step_seq as a string; the ordering key is now cast to an integer here, and the encoder emits it as an integer, so ordering is correct under either ingest typing. A dashboard already published under this title is never replaced by a re-run of quickstart.sh, so an existing factory keeps the query it first received — re-import this file by hand to pick up changes. CI has no backend, so none of this is re-verified automatically.

Attribute names are rewritten on ingest. Trace resource attributes are prefixed with 'service_' and every dot becomes an underscore, so af.formula_instance is queryable only as service_af_formula_instance. OTLP logs do NOT get the prefix, so the same attribute is af_formula_instance on the native-event side of the join. _timestamp is microseconds while start_time/end_time are nanoseconds and duration is microseconds.
duration is reported in microseconds, so the column is divided by 1000 to render milliseconds.

dashboard.title: Step duration by formula run
dashboard.description: How long each step took, in order.

queries.query:
SELECT service_af_formula_instance AS formula_run,
       service_af_agent            AS agent,
       CAST(af_step_seq AS BIGINT) AS step_order,
       af_step_id                  AS step,
       af_step_title               AS step_name,
       af_model                    AS model,
       af_status                   AS outcome,
       start_time                  AS started_at_ns,
       end_time                    AS ended_at_ns,
       duration / 1000             AS duration_ms
FROM "traces"."default"
WHERE service_name = 'agentfactory'
  AND af_step_id <> ''
ORDER BY service_af_formula_instance, CAST(af_step_seq AS BIGINT)
